conclusion: Repeated interaction routinely produces structure absent from the one-shot game: reputations, norms, conventions, and other institutions. The problem is to say what this structure is, when the bare game predicts play, and where the extra structure comes from. This paper argues that the institutional content of repeated play is a strict extension of the stage game: a refinement with genuinely new predictive distinctions not definable as a function of the game's own vocabulary. The argument uses a finite, fully explicit repeated-game laboratory, with mathematical claims verified by exact finite recomputation and reproducible validators, and a pre-registered re-analysis of a published human repeated Prisoner's Dilemma dataset. The institutional state studied here has a canonical form: the coarsest predictive summary of history, equivalent to a predictive-sufficiency or causal-state construction. On the finite carrier this object is non-definable from the game itself, and the predictive failure of stage-vocabulary models is priced exactly by a conditional mutual information. The quantitative constants governing institutional collapse are reproducible within declared protocols but resist shortcut: across a declared formula class and three frozen out-of-sample transfer attempts, no tested low-complexity shortcut transfers across families. In the human data, the corresponding predictive-residue hypothesis is confirmed out of sample under a protocol registered before any data access, while a more specific pre-registered timing hypothesis fails in the reverse direction: history-dependence grows with experience. Claims are scoped to the declared finite carrier, declared run families and protocols, and analyzed dataset; broader framework theorems are imported and cited, not re-proved here.

This calls for an explicit anti-relabeling stance.  This paper does not claim
the folk theorems, global games, reputation models, stochastic stability,
correlated equilibrium, Bayesian types, Markov states, or causal-state
quotients as its own results.  Those literatures are reference points: each
shows a way in which additional structure can matter.  The contribution here is the
certified inter-layer account that connects them without collapsing them into
one another: a canonical predictive institution, exact information-theoretic
price, finite non-definability certificates, material-feedback tests, and a
registered run/data program.  The strict-extension, predictive-quotient, and
closure-deficit theorem layers are imported from the cited source papers and
instantiated here on the declared carrier
\citep{Tsiokos2026CantorShell,
Tsiokos2026CastStone,Tsiokos2026NoGo}.  The precise novelty conjunction is
deferred to \Cref{sec:final-gate}, after the carrier, run-layer, and data results are

conclusion: It does not assert universal forcing.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
An example of the successful label is a recent-deviation bit: it can be on
because a defection occurred in the last two completed profiles, and then turn
off after two clean rounds.  This is public and history-computable, but it is
not merely the current stage profile or the empirical count summary.  Because
the trigger can be live at the comparison round, two histories that look
the same through the base game can lead extended strategies to different
future laws.  The landed exhibit holds relative to
the declared extension.  Its institutional reading is narrow:
publishing institutional state can change behavior broadly, but it enriches
the institution itself only under specific conditions--live,
non-stage-definable, reactive feedback--and, on this carrier, only where the
structure is still forming.  It does not assert universal forcing.

conclusion: The anti-relabeling ledger is part of the result. This paper does not claim the predictive-state or causal-state quotient construction as new; that is a standard way to summarize a process by its predictive consequences . It does not claim the closure-deficit identity, or the optimality of the best autonomous macro-predictor, as new; those are imported from the closure-deficit and no-go accounts . It does not claim the strict-extension, saturation, or promotion-obligation framework as new; those are imported standards for recognizing when a higher vocabulary is a genuine layer rather than a relabeling . Nor does it claim as new the game-theoretic fact that added structure matters. Folk theorems show that repeated interaction can support many outcomes; global games show how noisy private information can select; reputation models show how type structure changes play; evolutionary and stochastic-stability models show that convention selection can be a property of a run; correlated equilibrium and type spaces show how signals and hidden state enlarge the game . These are reference points the paper uses, not results it rebrands. The contribution is the conjunction, on one explicit repeated-game object, under one evidentiary discipline. First, the paper installs the predictive state as the canonical institution of repeated play and verifies, on the finite carrier, that it is not definable from the game's own stage vocabulary: the institutional partition strictly refines the stage partition and does not factor through it. Second, the paper prices the omission exactly by closure deficit, with a gap–residual decomposition that separates what conditioning on the institution recovers from what remains unpredictable even after that conditioning. Third, it assembles these facts into a certified strict-extension object: the institutional vocabulary saturates, admits an active label-feedback exhibit under a declared extension, and passes the admissibility gates for a promoted layer on the carrier. Fourth, the picture is subjected to tests that could have failed silently but were reported in full: the run-layer constants are reproducible within protocol yet fail three frozen out-of-sample transfer attempts, and the human-data analysis confirms the predictive-residue hypothesis while reversing the proposed timing bridge. The registered negatives are not qualifications to the result; they are part of the evidence for the strict-extension reading.

This conjunction also answers the three questions posed at the start, within
the declared scope.  What is an institution?  In this paper it is the canonical
predictive state of repeated play: the coarsest history summary sufficient for
the declared future.  When does the bare game predict behavior?  Exactly when
the stage vocabulary is closed, equivalently when its closure deficit is zero;
when the deficit is positive, the missing predictive information has an exact
price.  Where does the structure come from?  On the finite carrier, it appears
where the stage layer discards predictive information, can be made active only
under live non-stage-definable feedback, and produces run constants that are
reachable by running the process rather than by the tested low-complexity
shortcuts.  In the analyzed data, the corresponding residue is present, while
its timing points away from the fixed-population formation picture and toward
acquisition with experience.  These statements are scoped to the declared
carrier, declared run families and protocols, and the analyzed dataset; the
broader framework theorems are imported and cited, not re-proved here.

conclusion: Outlook.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Outlook.}
The most direct next construction is a within-agent learning or acquisition
carrier, in which the individual agent is treated as a carrier object in the
sense of the Six Birds treatment of agency \citep{Tsiokos2026ThrowStone}.  The
failed crystallization bridge in
\Cref{subsec:crystallization-bridge} shows that experience-as-composition
selection makes the finite carrier more homogeneous and more stage-predictable,
whereas the data show history-dependence growing with experience.  A carrier
in which individual agents acquire conditional rules over their own histories
would test the mechanism that this contrast leaves open.  A second direction
is a broader family of noisy and dissipative carriers, to map route memory
beyond the tested noise grid and to learn when currentizable traces become
genuinely coherent.  A third is to enlarge the strategic and payoff substrate:
richer automata, larger action spaces, asymmetric games, and longer public
signals would test which carrier facts persist and which are artifacts of the
minimal catalog.

conclusion: The most direct next construction is a within-agent learning or acquisition carrier, in which the individual agent is treated as a carrier object in the sense of the Six Birds treatment of agency . The failed crystallization bridge in shows that experience-as-composition selection makes the finite carrier more homogeneous and more stage-predictable, whereas the data show history-dependence growing with experience. A carrier in which individual agents acquire conditional rules over their own histories would test the mechanism that this contrast leaves open. A second direction is a broader family of noisy and dissipative carriers, to map route memory beyond the tested noise grid and to learn when currentizable traces become genuinely coherent. A third is to enlarge the strategic and payoff substrate: richer automata, larger action spaces, asymmetric games, and longer public signals would test which carrier facts persist and which are artifacts of the minimal catalog. The run layer also invites a bounded-rationality connection. The imitation dynamics used here contain a logit-style temperature parameter; in a maximum-entropy or shadow-price reading, such a parameter can be interpreted as the dual of a binding cognitive or informational budget rather than a free behavioral knob . That connection is only an opening in this paper, but it suggests how run-only constants might be tied to explicit resource constraints. On the empirical side, the immediate extension is broader pre-registered testing of the residue hypothesis and the timing reversal on other repeated-game datasets, with the same discipline: hypotheses, predictors, bands, folds, and amendments fixed before outcome analysis.
